To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fire can have a significant impact on the composition of high altitude grassland communities, and on mycorrhizae and soil properties.

(1) the most remarkable change in vegetation after fire was an abrupt increase of Festucatrichophylla in burnt area; (2) arbuscular mycorrizas were the most widespread mycorrhizae in all three grassland; (3) the AM colonization of F.trichophylla decreased in burnt area, but the AM colonization of Nardusstricta increased; (4) the phosphorus content of soil increased in burnt area.
The herbaceous vegetation of PNSE high altitude grassland are rather poor in number of species, but the number may be increase after fire.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early effects of fires on the herbaceous vegetation and the mycorrhiza symbiosis.
the early effects of a severe fire on the herbaceous vegetation and on the mycorrhiza symbiosis of a high altitude grassland ecosystem in Portugal.
the effects of fire on the herbaceous vegetation and on mycorrhizae symbiosis in high mountain ecosystems of PNSE.

fire has a positive effect on the vegetation and mycorhrizal symbiosis of the high altitude grasslands.
the fire in high altitude grass lands of PNSE has had an important impact on the herbaceous vegetation, the AM symbiosis and soil properties.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high altitude grasslands are very sensitive to fire.
the fire has a strong impact on the plant community and mycorrhiza symbiosis, which in turn may have consequences for the functioning of the ecosystem.
the fire in PNSE has had a significant impact on the herbaceous vegetation and AM symbiosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fire may have a significant role in maintaining the biodiversity of these high altitude grasslands and that the effects of fires are more complex than previously thought.
fires may be a key process to shape the high altitude grasslands in PNSE.
the high altitude grasslands are resilient to fire disturbance, but the effects on plant species composition and on mycorrhizae are important to understand the functioning of these ecosystems.
